userStories.title: Run the story workflow on the step graph
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Run the story workflow on the G1 step graph engine while preserving the story loop's observable behavior.

**Motivation** — The story loop is the last workflow machine still written as a hand-rolled loop.

**Approach** — A mechanical port, not a redesign. Every helper keeps its body: the same seam calls, ledger writes,
`sink.update` patches and `startStep` lines on stage `workflow`, in the same order. What changes:

1. The loop's in-memory state, today the `LoopState` class plus the locals `firstAfterResume` and `rulings`,
   becomes the graph state `StoryLoopState` (below), threaded through the engine.
2. The code between two decision points becomes one node's `run` function, returning
   `StepResult<StoryLoopState>`: a patch of the state keys it changed, and an exit label where it chose between
   destinations.
3. `runStoryLoop` builds the initial state and makes one `_storyLoopDeps.runStepGraph(...)` call.

The story loop differs from the feature workflow in three ways that shape the wiring, all of them pinned by
the G0 story goldens, which trace every `steps.costExceeded` call and every `sink.update` patch:

- **Persistence stays where it is.** The story record (`WorkflowStoryRecord`) is written by patches at fixed
  points inside the phases, not once per step. The nodes keep writing exactly those patches through
  `env.sink.update`. `StoryLoopState` is never persisted: the engine's `persist` hook is a no-op, and a resumed
  story is rebuilt from `env.resume` exactly as `LoopState`'s constructor rebuilds it today. A per-node persist
  would add `sink.update` calls the goldens do not have.
- **The cost limit is checked at two points, not before every agent step.** Today the loop calls
  `env.steps.costExceeded()` at the top of each evaluate pass and again before each fix round, and never before
  the first implement turn or the residual adjudication. The engine's own rule (ask `options.costExceeded()`
  before every `agent` node) would add calls. So the graph's `costStop` holds the story rule and reads
  `env.steps.costExceeded()` itself for the `evaluate` and `fix` nodes only, and `runStoryLoop` passes
  `costExceeded: () => true`, which hands every `agent` node to that `costStop` without a seam call of its own.
- **There is no abort check inside the loop.** The pipeline stage checks `ctx.abortSignal` after the loop
  returns (`src/workflow/stage.ts`). `runStoryLoop` passes `aborted: () => false` and no `onAbort`.

`runStoryLoop` keeps its name, its signature (`(env: StoryLoopEnv) => Promise<StoryLoopOutcome>`) and its
module, so `workflowStage`, `recordStoryTrace` (`test/helpers/workflow-story-trace.ts`) and every existing test
reach the ported code unchanged.

### State

```ts
// src/workflow/story-loop.ts
export type StoryNode = "implement" | "evaluate" | "residual" | "fix" | "close" | "done";

/** The story loop's working state; in memory only, never persisted (the record is written by patches). */
export interface StoryLoopState extends GraphState<StoryNode> {
  readonly round: number;
  readonly reviewed: boolean;
  readonly unreviewed: boolean;
  readonly nextId: number;
  readonly reviewOpen: readonly WorkflowFinding[];
  readonly pendingSession: readonly WorkflowFinding[];
  readonly concerns: readonly string[];
  readonly questions: number;
  readonly deferredMinors: number;
  readonly fixBase?: string;
  readonly gates?: GateRunResult;
  readonly suite?: GateRunResult;
  readonly suiteThisIteration: boolean;
  /** Set by the graph's cost stop; read by `close` through `deriveEndState`. */
  readonly costLimited: boolean;
  /** The first fix round after a resume runs fresh. */
  readonly firstAfterResume: boolean;
  /** The current evaluate pass's open findings (gate, review or suite, plus pending session findings). */
  readonly open: readonly WorkflowFinding[];
  readonly rulings: readonly WorkflowRuling[];
  /** Set by `implement` when the no-work ladder closes the story; `close` uses it instead of `deriveEndState`. */
  readonly closeAs?: { readonly state: WorkflowEndState; readonly reason: string };
  /** Set by `close`; what `runStoryLoop` resolves to. */
  readonly outcome?: StoryLoopOutcome;
}
```

`initialStoryState(env)` builds the starting state with the same rules `LoopState`'s constructor uses today:
`round`, `reviewed`, `unreviewed`, `deferredMinors` and `fixBase` from `env.resume` (defaults `0`, `false`,
`false`, `0`, absent), `nextId` from `env.resume.nextFindingId` (default `1`), `reviewOpen` from the resume
record's `openFindings` filtered to kinds `spec` and `quality`, `pendingSession`, `concerns`, `open` and
`rulings` empty, `questions` `0`, `suiteThisIteration` and `costLimited` `false`, `firstAfterResume` equal to
`env.resume !== null`, `timings` `{}`, and `step` `"implement"` for a fresh story (`env.resume === null`) or
`"evaluate"` for a resumed one. A resumed story skips the first implement turn, as `openStory` does today.

A node never mutates the state object it is handed (the engine's contract). Inside one node the helpers may
keep working on a node-local mutable copy: today's `LoopState` class, moved to `story-steps.ts` and built from
the graph state at the start of the node instead of from `env.resume`. The node then returns every key it
declares in `produces`, read off that copy, as its patch (so a key whose value is unchanged is restated, and a
key the copy holds as `undefined`, such as a retired `fixBase`, is cleared). The helpers keep their bodies and
their `s: LoopState` parameter. The copy gains no fields: it holds what `LoopState` holds today, with its
`costStop` field read from the state's `costLimited`, while `open`, `rulings`, `firstAfterResume` and `closeAs`
are node locals read from and patched onto the graph state directly.

### File layout

`story-loop.ts` splits into three files, each under the 600-line limit `check:file-sizes` enforces:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `src/workflow/story-loop.ts` | `StoryLoopSteps`, `StoryLoopSink`, `StoryLoopEnv`, `StoryLoopOutcome`, `StoryNode`, `StoryLoopState`, `_storyLoopDeps`, `runStoryLoop` (the wiring below), and a re-export of `turnLabel` from `story-steps.ts`, so `stage-env.ts` and `story-loop.test.ts` keep importing it from `./story-loop`. |
| `src/workflow/story-steps.ts` (new) | The five node functions (`implementStep`, `evaluateStep`, `residualStep`, `fixStep`, `closeStep`), `initialStoryState`, and everything else moved from `story-loop.ts`: the `LoopState` class and the `TurnOrigin` interface (the helpers' working copy, see § State), the helpers `implementTurn`, `absorbTurn`, `recordConcern`, `review`, `reReviewStatus`, `reReviewSummary`, `deferMinors`, `evaluate`, `redGateNames`, `closeLoop`, `NO_MIRROR`, `isBlocking`, the exported constants `WARM_ROUND_CAP` and `MAX_IMPLEMENTER_QUESTIONS` (no module outside the story loop imports them, so they are not re-exported), and `turnLabel`. Imports from `story-loop.ts` are type-only. |
| `src/workflow/story-graph.ts` (new) | `STORY_GRAPH` and its `costStop`. |

Import direction: `story-loop.ts` -> `story-graph.ts` -> `story-steps.ts` (values), `story-loop.ts` ->
`story-steps.ts` (values: `initialStoryState` and the re-exports), and `story-steps.ts` -> `story-loop.ts`
(types only), so `check:import-cycles` sees no runtime cycle. `no-work.ts` keeps its type-only import of
`StoryLoopEnv` from `./story-loop`. The workflow imports the engine through its barrel, `@/step-graph`.
`STORY_GRAPH` is declared with an explicit type,
`export const STORY_GRAPH: StepGraph<StoryLoopState, StoryLoopEnv, StoryNode> = defineStepGraph({ ... })`, for
the same reason G2 annotates `FEATURE_GRAPH`: without it `kind` and `start` widen to `string`. Tests reach
`STORY_GRAPH.costStop` with `?.(...)` and nodes through a small accessor that throws on a missing node, never a
non-null `!` (a biome error) or a cast.

### Node table

`STORY_GRAPH`: `start` `"implement"`, `end` `["done"]`, `costStopProduces` `["costLimited"]`. No node declares
`needs` and the graph declares no `inputs` (see Out of Scope). No node declares `commits`: the story loop keeps
no `lastHead`, and `runStoryLoop` passes no `readHead`.

| Node | `kind` | Body (today's code) | `produces` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `implement` | `agent` | `openStory` up to and including `absorbTurn`: `sink.update({ phase: "implement" })`, the first implementer turn, `runNoWorkLadder`, `absorbTurn` | `pendingSession`, `nextId`, `questions`, `concerns`, `closeAs` |
| `evaluate` | `agent` | one loop pass up to the two decisions: `evaluate`, the open list with `pendingSession` folded in and cleared, and the `sink.update` of `openFindings`, `fixBase`, `reviewed`, `unreviewed`, `nextFindingId`, `deferredMinors` | `suiteThisIteration`, `gates`, `suite`, `nextId`, `reviewed`, `unreviewed`, `deferredMinors`, `reviewOpen`, `fixBase`, `open`, `pendingSession` |
| `residual` | `agent` | the `round >= maxFixRounds` branch: `sink.update({ phase: "residual" })`, the full suite when the gates were green and the suite did not run this pass, `adjudicateResidual` over the non-gate open items | `suite`, `rulings` |
| `fix` | `agent` | one fix round: `round` incremented, `fresh` (`round > warm` or the first round after a resume), `firstAfterResume` cleared, `fixBase` read from `head()` when review findings are open and no base is held, the `fixRound` ledger line, `sink.update({ phase: "fix", round, fixBase })`, the fix turn, `absorbTurn` | `round`, `firstAfterResume`, `fixBase`, `pendingSession`, `nextId`, `questions`, `concerns` |
| `close` | `pure` | `deriveEndState` (or `closeAs` when set) then `closeLoop` | `outcome` |

`close` writes only through the sink (the record patch and the end ledger line); it makes no agent, git, gate
or forge call, so its kind is `pure`. Each `produces` list is every state key the node's code can change.

### Transitions

| Node | Exit | Returned when (today's code path) | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| `implement` | `worked` | the no-work ladder did not close the story | `evaluate` |
| `implement` | `no-work` | the ladder closed it (`result.closed`); the patch sets `closeAs` to `{ state: "complete-gate-open", reason: "no work produced" }` | `close` |
| `evaluate` | `clean` | the open list is empty | `close` |
| `evaluate` | `capped` | findings are open and `round >= maxFixRounds` | `residual` |
| `evaluate` | `open` | findings are open and a fix round is left | `fix` |
| `residual` | — | always | `close` |
| `fix` | — | always | `evaluate` |
| `close` | — | always | `done` |

### Cost stop

`STORY_GRAPH.costStop(node, state, env)`. The engine calls it for every `agent` node, because `runStoryLoop`
passes `costExceeded: () => true`. For `implement` and `residual` it resolves to `undefined` without calling
`env.steps.costExceeded`. For `evaluate` and `fix` it calls `env.steps.costExceeded()` once; when that returns
true it resolves to `{ patch: { costLimited: true }, to: "close" }`, otherwise to `undefined`. It writes no log
line, no ledger line and no record patch, as the loop's `break` writes none today.

### Wiring `runStoryLoop`

```ts
// src/workflow/story-loop.ts
/** The engine call, typed for this graph so a test can stub it without a cast. */
type RunStoryGraph = (
  graph: typeof STORY_GRAPH,
  env: StoryLoopEnv,
  state: StoryLoopState,
  hooks: StepGraphHooks<StoryLoopState, StoryNode>,
  options: StepGraphRunOptions<StoryNode>,
) => Promise<StoryLoopState>;

export const _storyLoopDeps: { runStepGraph: RunStoryGraph } = { runStepGraph };

export async function runStoryLoop(env: StoryLoopEnv): Promise<StoryLoopOutcome> {
  const final = await _storyLoopDeps.runStepGraph(
    STORY_GRAPH,
    env,
    initialStoryState(env),
    // The story record is written by the nodes' own sink patches; the graph state is never persisted.
    { persist: async () => {} },
    // The story loop has no abort check of its own, and its cost rule lives in STORY_GRAPH.costStop.
    { aborted: () => false, now: () => Date.now(), costExceeded: () => true },
  );
  if (final.outcome === undefined) {
    throw new NaxError("The story workflow ended without an outcome", "WORKFLOW_STORY_NO_OUTCOME", {
      stage: "workflow",
      storyId: env.storyId,
    });
  }
  return final.outcome;
}
```

`logScope` stays unset: the helpers write their own `workflow` lines, which the G0 goldens pin, and the engine
then logs nothing. `onStep`, `readHead` and `onAbort` are not passed. The shape above is the target; helper names
other than the ones it uses are the builder's.

### Integration

Symbols this feature changes. Each **Baseline** exists only to locate today's code and is never the interface to
implement; implement the **Target**.

- `runStoryLoop` in `src/workflow/story-loop.ts`.
  - Baseline: `async function runStoryLoop(env: StoryLoopEnv): Promise<StoryLoopOutcome>`, a `for (;;)` loop over
    a `LoopState`, with `openStory` before it and `closeLoop` after.
  - Target: same signature; the body is the `_storyLoopDeps.runStepGraph(...)` call above.
- The loop state.
  - Baseline: `class LoopState` (not exported) plus the locals `firstAfterResume` and `rulings` in `runStoryLoop`.
  - Target: `StoryLoopState` (exported type) threaded through the engine, built by `initialStoryState`.
- `WARM_ROUND_CAP`, `MAX_IMPLEMENTER_QUESTIONS`, `turnLabel`.
  - Baseline: declared and exported in `story-loop.ts`.
  - Target: declared and exported in `story-steps.ts`; only `turnLabel` is re-exported from `story-loop.ts`.
- `LoopState` and `TurnOrigin`.
  - Baseline: in `story-loop.ts`; `LoopState`'s constructor takes the resume record.
  - Target: in `story-steps.ts`; `LoopState` is built from a `StoryLoopState` (the node-local working copy).
- Removed from `story-loop.ts` with nothing in their place: `openStory` (its body is the `implement` node) and the
  loop body (the `evaluate`, `residual` and `fix` nodes).

Symbols read and not changed (verified on `main` @ `d46d5631d`):

- `runStepGraph`, `defineStepGraph`, `validateStepGraph`, and the types `GraphState`, `StepGraph`, `StepResult`,
  `CostStop`, `StepGraphHooks`, `StepGraphRunOptions` — `@/step-graph`.
- `StoryLoopSteps`, `StoryLoopSink`, `StoryLoopEnv`, `StoryLoopOutcome` — `src/workflow/story-loop.ts` (stay
  there, unchanged).
- `runNoWorkLadder` — `src/workflow/no-work.ts`; `deriveEndState` — `src/workflow/close.ts`;
  `adjudicateResidual` — `src/workflow/adjudicate.ts`; `absorbReReviewVerdict` —
  `src/workflow/re-review-absorb.ts`; `ledgerCannotVerify` — `src/workflow/gate-timing.ts`; `ledgerText` —
  `src/workflow/ledger.ts`; `startStep`, `describeFindings` — `src/workflow/run-log.ts`.
- `WorkflowStoryRecord`, `WorkflowFinding`, `WorkflowRuling`, `WorkflowEndState`, `GateRunResult` —
  `src/workflow/types.ts`.
- `workflowStage` and `_workflowStageDeps` — `src/workflow/stage.ts`; `buildStoryEnv` —
  `src/workflow/stage-env.ts` (both unchanged).
- `recordStoryTrace` — `test/helpers/workflow-story-trace.ts`; `makeStoryLoopHarness`, `storyLoopFixtures`,
  `failingReview` — `test/helpers/workflow-story-loop.ts`.
- The G2 precedent to mirror: `FEATURE_GRAPH` in `src/workflow/feature-graph.ts` and `_featureMachineDeps` /
  `runFeatureMachine` in `src/workflow/feature-machine.ts`.

### Equivalence evidence

The port is correct when today's tests pass without a single edit. In particular:

- `test/unit/workflow/story-loop-equivalence.test.ts` replays all twelve G0 story scenarios through
  `runStoryLoop` and compares them with the committed goldens in `test/fixtures/workflow-equivalence/story/`,
  including every `costExceeded` call and every `sink.update` patch.
- `story-loop.test.ts` (including the cost check before a fix round), `story-loop-log.test.ts`,
  `story-loop-no-work.test.ts`, `step-models-log.test.ts`, `stage.test.ts`, `stage-env.test.ts`,
  `adjudicate-close.test.ts` and `test/integration/workflow/stage-env-work-produced.test.ts` cover the paths the
  goldens do not.

None of those files and no golden changes (see `### Modifies`). A difference in any of them is a behaviour
change and a defect in the port, never a fixture to refresh.

### Failure Handling

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| A seam call or helper throws inside a node | The error propagates out of `runStoryLoop` unchanged, and `workflowStage` closes the story gate-open as today. The engine catches nothing from a node. |
| The cost limit is reached at the top of an evaluate pass or before a fix round | The `costStop` routes to `close` with `costLimited` true; `close` derives `complete-gate-open` / `cost-limit` (as today). |
| The graph ends with no `outcome` on the final state | `runStoryLoop` rejects with `NaxError` `WORKFLOW_STORY_NO_OUTCOME`, context `{ stage: "workflow", storyId }`. Unreachable through `STORY_GRAPH` (`done` is reached only from `close`); it exists so the return needs no non-null assertion. |
| A node patches a key its node does not declare | Rejects with `STEP_GRAPH_UNDECLARED_OUTPUT`. A programming error the node table rules out; the existing suites exercise every patch. |

**Scope** — In: modify only `packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts`; create `packages/nax/src/workflow/story-steps.ts`, `packages/nax/src/workflow/story-graph.ts`, `packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/story-graph.test.ts` and `packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/story-loop-graph.test.ts`. Implementation includes helper extraction, immutable node adapters, graph declarations, runner wiring and graph/wiring tests. Read existing callers, engine, helpers and tests for compatibility without modifying them. No inter-story exclusions: this is the feature's only story.

**Scope** — Out:
- Persisting the graph cursor or `StoryLoopState`, or adding `step` to `WorkflowStoryRecord`: the story record's shape and its write points stay as they are, and a resumed story starts at `evaluate` as today.
- Checking the cost limit before every agent node (the engine's default rule) in the story workflow: that would add cost checks before the first implement turn and the residual adjudication, a behaviour change; a later phase may adopt it deliberately.
- An abort check inside the story workflow: the pipeline stage keeps checking `ctx.abortSignal` after `runStoryLoop` returns.
- Splitting the no-work ladder (`runNoWorkLadder`), the implementer question loop in `absorbTurn`, or the warm/fresh round rule into graph nodes of their own: they stay inside the `implement` and `fix` nodes.
- Declaring `needs` on the story nodes and `inputs` on the graph: settled in G4, with the narrow step context.
- A narrow step context, a PR context, and running any story step outside a nax run: G4.
- Setting `logScope` for the story graph, or any new log line, ledger line, record field, record patch or outcome field: the port is behaviour-identical.
- Changing `workflowStage` (`src/workflow/stage.ts`), `buildStoryEnv` (`src/workflow/stage-env.ts`) or `runNoWorkLadder` (`src/workflow/no-work.ts`).
- Editing any existing test file or any golden under `test/fixtures/workflow-equivalence/`, or regenerating goldens with `NAX_UPDATE_WORKFLOW_GOLDEN=1`: the unchanged suites are the equivalence evidence.
- Changing the step graph engine (`src/step-graph/`) or the feature workflow files (`feature-graph.ts`, `feature-steps.ts`, `feature-machine.ts`).
- The deprecated `src/finish/` phase and pipeline mode: pipeline mode is frozen.
- The live-run check the master plan requires for G3 (one real `nax run` on the new build matching the old build): a manual step after merge, run only with the user's approval, not story work.
- Release notes, user docs and a release: the port has no user-visible surface.

**Interface** — Implement the verbatim `StoryNode`, `StoryLoopState`, `RunStoryGraph`, `_storyLoopDeps` and `runStoryLoop` declarations above. Keep `StoryLoopSteps`, `StoryLoopSink`, `StoryLoopEnv` and `StoryLoopOutcome` unchanged in `src/workflow/story-loop.ts`. `STORY_GRAPH` is exported from `src/workflow/story-graph.ts`; `initialStoryState` and the five node functions are exported from `src/workflow/story-steps.ts`. Only `turnLabel` is re-exported from the steps module by `story-loop.ts`.

Verification note: the removals are checked by the build and static gates (`bun run typecheck`,
`bun run check:all`, which runs `check:file-sizes` and `check:import-cycles`), and the existing suites listed in
Design § Equivalence evidence pass unchanged. `bun run test:coverage` covers the two new source files.

Test implementation belongs in the two new files only. Exercise graph data, cost stop and nodes in story-graph.test.ts; exercise wiring and initial state in story-loop-graph.test.ts, including the real engine path. Save and restore `_storyLoopDeps.runStepGraph` after every stubbed test, following feature-machine-graph.test.ts. Do not use `NAX_UPDATE_WORKFLOW_GOLDEN=1`.

Codebase-fit clarification: the node invocation signature is `run(env: StoryLoopEnv, state: StoryLoopState): Promise<StepResult<StoryLoopState>>`, while the graph cost hook is `costStop(node, state, env)`. Direct node tests must pass arguments in those different orders. Build valid node-test states from `initialStoryState(env)` plus the specified overrides; in the close-override case this retains `unreviewed: false`. Error propagation means errors escaping existing helper handling: `adjudicateResidual` already catches advisor failures and defaults to hold, and that helper body must remain unchanged. The stage's gate-open failure behavior refers to a built environment and a non-aborted context; its existing abort rethrow remains outside this loop. Failure-mode evidence may reuse the unchanged stage and engine suites. Any additional negative-case test belongs in one of the two new test files; exercising undeclared output must use a test-local graph value, never mutate STORY_GRAPH or change the engine. The normalized trace equality requirement is behavioral compatibility evidence, not permission to edit existing scenarios or refresh fixtures.

analysis:
Goal and scope: mechanically port the existing story workflow to the G1 step graph engine without changing observable story behavior. This is an existing-code refactor in @nathapp/nax, not a new workflow or a redesign. The binding structure is exactly US-001, workdir packages/nax, no dependencies. Graph-first navigation was unavailable because this host exposes no codebase-memory MCP tools; findings below come from direct source reads and searches.

Current implementation: packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:33-80 defines the public StoryLoopSteps, StoryLoopSink, StoryLoopEnv and StoryLoopOutcome contracts that must stay in this module unchanged. LoopState at packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:87-116 owns round, review status, finding IDs, review and session findings, concerns, question count, deferred minors, fix base, gate/suite results and cost-stop state. Its constructor rebuilds resume state and filters open findings to spec/quality. turnLabel at packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:123 is a public compatibility surface. The helpers implementTurn, absorbTurn, recordConcern, review, re-review summaries, deferMinors, evaluate, redGateNames and closeLoop are orchestration over injected seams, not new I/O sites. The review helper at packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:192 retires fixBase after re-review; evaluate at packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:253 writes gates/review/suite phase patches in a fixed order and skips review on red gates. The existing loop begins at packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:273. It calls openStory before looping, checks cost at line 284 before evaluation, folds in and clears pendingSession, writes openFindings and review bookkeeping at line 290, branches to residual at line 300, checks cost again at line 311 before a fix, increments round and computes fresh at lines 315-317, then records the fix ledger and sink patch at line 326 before running the implementer. openStory at line 346 skips implementation on resume and keeps the no-work ladder and absorbTurn before early close. closeLoop at line 356 writes the closed record before the end ledger and returns the existing outcome shape.

Engine integration: packages/nax/src/step-graph/types.ts:16-121 provides GraphState, StepResult, StepNode, StepGraph, cost-stop, hooks and options contracts. State.step, timings and optional lastHead are engine-owned. StepResult.patch clears a key when its value is undefined; nodes must restate all declared output keys, including retired optional values. The engine checks node output declarations at packages/nax/src/step-graph/run.ts:76, applies patches to a copy at line 150, asks the graph cost stop only for agent nodes when the options predicate is true at lines 232-244, awaits node.run without wrapping its error at line 271, and invokes persist after every executed or cost-stopped node at line 302. runStepGraph at line 311 starts from state.step rather than graph.start, enabling resumed stories to start at evaluate. Engine logging is gated by logScope at line 194. Therefore use a no-op persist hook, no logScope, aborted returning false, and costExceeded returning true without consulting the story seam. The graph costStop alone calls env.steps.costExceeded once for evaluate/fix and never for implement/residual. No commits declarations or readHead injection: the story's existing explicit head() call for fixBase remains inside fixStep. Import the engine only through @/step-graph.

Precedent and dependencies: packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-graph.ts:19 explicitly types FEATURE_GRAPH with StepGraph and uses defineStepGraph; mirror that typing to avoid widened kind/start literals, but do not copy its different persistence, cost logging, commit bookkeeping or abort behavior. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts:72-101 defines a concrete runner function type, _featureMachineDeps and a thin engine adapter. packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature-machine-graph.test.ts:11-13 saves/restores the injectable runner after each test; use the same isolation for _storyLoopDeps. The new value import direction is story-loop -> story-graph -> story-steps, with story-loop also importing initialStoryState and re-exporting turnLabel from story-steps; story-steps imports story-loop contracts as types only. There must be no runtime cycle.

Compatibility and impact: packages/nax/src/workflow/stage.ts:15 imports runStoryLoop and line 19 exposes it through _workflowStageDeps. The production call is at line 50; line 52 checks abort only after the story loop returns; lines 59-65 retain the existing gate-open error handling. Do not modify stage.ts. packages/nax/src/workflow/stage-env.ts:24 imports StoryLoopEnv, StoryLoopSteps and turnLabel; packages/nax/src/workflow/no-work.ts:17 and packages/nax/src/workflow/step-model.ts:20 import story-loop types. packages/nax/test/helpers/workflow-story-trace.ts:14 records behavior through the existing entry point and seam types. Re-exporting turnLabel, preserving the entry-point signature and retaining the four public interfaces avoids caller migration. Only packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts is modified; four files are created: story-steps.ts, story-graph.ts and the two new graph-focused unit test files. No engine, feature workflow, stage environment, no-work helper, existing test helper, test or golden changes.

Implementation and migration sequence within the one story: write the two new test files first; introduce exported StoryNode/StoryLoopState and initialStoryState; move helpers and the original-field-only LoopState working copy into story-steps.ts; express implement/evaluate/residual/fix/close as immutable graph nodes that use node-local working copies and return their complete produces patches; add the explicitly typed STORY_GRAPH with exact transition order and the selective cost stop; replace runStoryLoop with its one injected engine call and explicit missing-outcome NaxError guard. Move constants without re-exporting WARM_ROUND_CAP or MAX_IMPLEMENTER_QUESTIONS, delete openStory and the handwritten loop, and re-export only turnLabel. This is an in-place port, not a dual-run migration or feature flag. Existing record formats and resume reconstruction stay unchanged, and no persisted cursor or graph timings are added.

Risks: extra sink writes from engine persistence, extra cost seam calls from the generic engine policy, engine-generated log lines, changed no-work close order, stale fixBase after re-review, lost pending session findings, duplicate finding IDs, mutation of readonly graph state through array aliases, changed first-after-resume freshness or warm cap, and accidentally forcing full-suite execution on the wrong residual path. Copy mutable containers into LoopState, retain helper bodies and ordering, patch undefined outputs explicitly, and keep open/rulings/firstAfterResume/closeAs outside the working copy. Node-local copies must map costLimited to the existing costStop field so deriveEndState remains unchanged. The close node remains pure in graph classification even though it writes to the injected sink. Do not catch or translate seam/helper errors. New invariant failure is exactly WORKFLOW_STORY_NO_OUTCOME with message and context from the spec.

Test strategy: use bun:test and existing makeStoryLoopHarness, failingReview and storyLoopFixtures from packages/nax/test/helpers/workflow-story-loop.ts:54-237, imported via @test/helpers. The harness clones queued answers, records implement turns, ledger lines and sink patches, supports seam overrides, and independently copies resume records at lines 135-143 and 194-198. New story-graph.test.ts exercises graph declarations, cost stop, immutable node behavior, no-work, residual and close. New story-loop-graph.test.ts exercises fresh/resumed initial state, runner wiring, no-op persistence, options, missing outcome and a real-engine one-fix story. Restore _storyLoopDeps after each stubbed test; access optional costStop with ?. and use a throwing node accessor rather than casts/non-null assertions. The twelve existing story goldens are present under packages/nax/test/fixtures/workflow-equivalence/story/: clean, cost-exceeded, fresh-after-warm-cap, full-suite-red, needs-context-answered, no-work-restart, red-gates-then-green, rereview-new-finding, residual-rulings, resume-mid-fix, review-fail-one-round and review-not-ran. packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/story-loop-equivalence.test.ts:1-38 documents the seam-and-workflow-log recorder, and its scenarios assert exact committed traces. Existing story-loop.test.ts:327 pins cost before a fix and line 335 pins resume freshness and IDs. Preserve all existing tests, especially story-loop.test.ts, story-loop-log.test.ts, story-loop-no-work.test.ts, step-models-log.test.ts, stage.test.ts, stage-env.test.ts, adjudicate-close.test.ts and test/integration/workflow/stage-env-work-produced.test.ts. Never regenerate goldens. Run package-scoped targeted tests with explicit paths, then the usual typecheck/check:all/test pipeline; separately run bun run test:coverage after adding/moving tests because it is not part of the standard nax pipeline. Static gates cover file sizes (600 source-line hard limit), import cycles and removal-related build failures. Architecture reference: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:17-35 and :158-176 indexes _deps, error, testing and file-size conventions. No live nax run, release or documentation task is part of this implementation; live equivalence requires post-merge user approval.

Refine-pass audit against docs/specs/SPEC-step-graph-g3-story-port.md: all 20 numbered spec criteria are retained in US-001, with compound assertions split without changing their meaning. Explicit preservation map: spec 1 -> AC-01a/01b/01c (import, validation, start, end); 2 -> AC-02 (exact agent/pure kinds); 3 -> AC-03 (no commits true); 4 -> AC-04a/04b (all produces sets and cost outputs); 5 -> AC-05a/05b (ordered transitions, absent on and exact/absent exits); 6 -> AC-06a/06b/06c/06d (evaluate cost stop, one call, no sink writes); 7 -> AC-07a/07b (fix false/one call); 8 -> AC-08a/08b (implement/residual undefined without seam calls); 9 -> AC-09 (fresh defaults); 10 -> AC-10 (resume fields and finding filter); 11 -> AC-11a/11b (one runner call, initial cursor, returned outcome and restored stub); 12 -> AC-12a/12b/12c/12d (no-op persistence and no onStep); 13 -> AC-13a/13b/13c/13d/13e/13f (constant options, no cost seam read, absent optional hooks); 14 -> AC-14 (NaxError code/context); 15 -> AC-15a/15b (capped exit and unchanged input); 16 -> AC-16a/16b (own fresh harness, open exit and important finding); 17 -> AC-17a/17b (all three no-status turns, no work, no-work exit and close override); 18 -> AC-18a/18b (exact close outcome and one closed patch); 19 -> AC-19a/19b (unstubbed engine outcome and ordered implement/fix turns); 20 -> AC-20a/20b/20c/20d/20e (residual full suite, advisor items, no exit, suite and adjudicated rulings). Each preserves its specified harness, preconditions and qualifying clauses. All assertions are observable through graph property reads, call captures, promise results, input-state snapshots, error identity or normalized traces.

Failure-mode audit: all four failure-table rows remain represented (row 3 is AC-14). Clarify row 1 without changing existing handling: packages/nax/src/workflow/adjudicate.ts:16-23 already catches ruleResidual failures and defaults to hold, so unchanged propagation applies to errors escaping existing helper handling, not to errors already recovered there. packages/nax/src/workflow/stage.ts:59-66 closes gate-open only on its non-abort error path and calls the environment's closeOnError; packages/nax/src/workflow/stage-env.ts:168-183 writes state complete-gate-open, phase closed and the workflow-error reason best-effort. The revised stage assertion specifies that non-aborted, built-environment precondition and observable closeOnError call, retaining 'as today'. Existing stage tests at packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/stage.test.ts:250 and :266 cover contained errors and abort rethrow separately. The engine's undeclared-output refusal is observed through runStepGraph, not by expecting a directly invoked node.run to validate itself. Added the spec's explicit equivalence requirement as a trace-equality regression assertion rather than a test-pass or coverage gate.

Boundary and routing audit: all 13 feature-level exclusions remain verbatim in top-level outOfScope and are echoed verbatim in the story's Scope — Out section; there are no story-local deferrals to hoist. The scope now excludes the live-run check from story work even with approval, instead of implying approval makes it implementation work. The five contextFiles exactly match the spec's five existing recommended files; all four new paths remain only in expectedFiles. The sole story stays US-001, packages/nax, dependencies []. Routing is reduced to medium/tdd-simple: one 376-line loop is mechanically distributed across three production modules and two new test files, using established engine, harness and dependency-injection contracts rather than introducing a new abstraction or security-sensitive lifecycle capability. No source, existing test, helper, fixture or dependency changes were made during PRD refinement.
outOfScope: Persisting the graph cursor or `StoryLoopState`, or adding `step` to `WorkflowStoryRecord`: the story record's shape and its write points stay as they are, and a resumed story starts at `evaluate` as today.

Checking the cost limit before every agent node (the engine's default rule) in the story workflow: that would add cost checks before the first implement turn and the residual adjudication, a behaviour change; a later phase may adopt it deliberately.
An abort check inside the story workflow: the pipeline stage keeps checking `ctx.abortSignal` after `runStoryLoop` returns.

Splitting the no-work ladder (`runNoWorkLadder`), the implementer question loop in `absorbTurn`, or the warm/fresh round rule into graph nodes of their own: they stay inside the `implement` and `fix` nodes.
Declaring `needs` on the story nodes and `inputs` on the graph: settled in G4, with the narrow step context.
A narrow step context, a PR context, and running any story step outside a nax run: G4.
Setting `logScope` for the story graph, or any new log line, ledger line, record field, record patch or outcome field: the port is behaviour-identical.

Editing any existing test file or any golden under `test/fixtures/workflow-equivalence/`, or regenerating goldens with `NAX_UPDATE_WORKFLOW_GOLDEN=1`: the unchanged suites are the equivalence evidence.
Changing the step graph engine (`src/step-graph/`) or the feature workflow files (`feature-graph.ts`, `feature-steps.ts`, `feature-machine.ts`).
The deprecated `src/finish/` phase and pipeline mode: pipeline mode is frozen.
The live-run check the master plan requires for G3 (one real `nax run` on the new build matching the old build): a manual step after merge, run only with the user's approval, not story work.
Release notes, user docs and a release: the port has no user-visible surface.
